messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] prod-west.tokenizer.preproc.latency.p99 > 6s (threshold 2s) — pages sent to #incidents and on-call
Kayla: paging oncall for prod-west high tail latency, p99 is spiking, looks correlated with JSON-mode routes
Eli: on-call, taking this. initial glance: p95 ~1.2s but p99 hitting 6–9s, streaming tails seen as timeouts from clients. grabbing dashboards now
Kayla: thanks. I see a recent deploy to prompt-templates-service ~22m ago, could be related (template compiler change). also a config flip enabling full JSON mode parsing for /chat-tool route
Eli: confirmed. alert map: tokenizer queue depth +150, cpu on preproc hosts spiking to 90% for python-worker. metrics snippet:
```
metric: prod-west.tokenizer.latency p50=120ms p95=1.2s p99=6.8s
preproc_cpu: 88% (python-kvcache workers)
incoming_rps: +18% over baseline
json_mode_enabled_routes: ["/chat-tool", "/agent-json"]
```
Eli: adding mitigation checklist:
- stop JSON-mode parsing for /chat-tool
- increase preproc worker count on prod-west for safe capacity
- fallback streaming chunking to reduce end-to-end blocking
- roll back prompt-templates-service build if correlated
Kayla: I'm going to disable json_mode flag for /chat-tool now (low-risk toggle)
DeployBot: config-change: feature_flag.json_mode.disabled_routes updated -> added /chat-tool by Kayla (rollout 100%)
Eli: observed immediate drop in per-request preproc time for sampled traces. p99 fell from ~7.2s -> ~3.6s within 60s. good signal but still above SLO of 2s
Tony: can we revert that prompt-templates build? it did a shallow compile that introspects tool schemas at render-time — could be heavy when templates include large tool schemas
Miguel: I can roll back the build, but want to confirm correlation. Kayla, any logs from template service?
Kayla: grabbing logs now. saw repeated expensive calls:
```
2026-03-15T03:02:12Z prompt-templates[pid=2345] INFO compiling template id=ab12
2026-03-15T03:02:12Z prompt-templates[pid=2345] DEBUG schema-resolve tool_count=14 total_schema_size=1.7MB
2026-03-15T03:02:13Z prompt-templates[pid=2345] WARN render_time=1.1s
```
Kayla: templates that include tool schemas are adding ~1s on average to preproc per request. combined with tokenizer work it's pushing tail to 6–9s
Eli: plan: 1) keep json_mode disabled for /chat-tool 2) throttle incoming QPS for that route temporarily via rate-limiter 3) revert prompt-templates build (Miguel) 4) add short-term increased preproc workers 5) postmortem follow-up for template compilation caching
Miguel: rolling prompt-templates -> previous sha now. command:
```
git checkout f5a8d3 && kubectl set image deploy/prompt-templates prompt-templates=registry/redwood/prompt-templates:f5a8d3-prod
```
DeployBot: deploy triggered by Miguel -> prompt-templates rollout starting (replicas 4 -> 4)
Eli: applying rate-limit rule to /chat-tool: 20 rps per token bucket for 10m window to protect preproc. will monitor errors and latency
Tony: can we also enable template compilation cache (in-memory LRU) as a quick config instead of full revert? would shave ~0.8s from hot paths
Miguel: revert landed; seeing success rate up. p99 down to ~1.9s on controlled sample after 3 minutes.
Jules (Support): Support is seeing customer errors for 3 large customers (timeouts). I've opened tickets and notified account reps. customers affected by streaming stalls and timeouts; estimated ~1.2k requests failed in last 30m.
Eli: acknowledging. create incident severity update for customer comms. Kayla can you add impacted customers list + earliest observed failure time to the incident doc?
Kayla: done — added to incident doc (link internal) and pinged customer success.
Eli: monitoring: keep json_mode off for /chat-tool and /agent-json for now (until template caching is verified). temporally increase preproc pool by 30% across prod-west via ASG scale up requests.
Kayla: scale up request submitted to infra (tickets #INF-4521).
Miguel: toggled template cache flag on non-production to validate, will promote to prod after smoke. sequence: enable cache -> run canary 5% -> promote.
Eli: handoff: I'm heading offline in 25m. Miguel, you'll own overnight. summary for handoff:
- root cause: prompt-template change introduced runtime schema introspection on render path; combined with JSON-mode parsing this amplified preproc CPU and tokenizer queueing causing streaming tail latency and SLO breaches (p99 up to ~9s)
- mitigations applied: 1) disabled JSON-mode on /chat-tool 2) rate-limited route to 20rps 3) reverted prompt-templates build 4) scaled preproc workers up 30% 5) enabled template-cache canary (miguel)
- current status: p99 ~1.9s on sampling, system stable, incoming errors trending down, customers still have residual failed requests; support engaged
- next steps: promote cache canary, instrument compile-time histograms to detect template-heavy renders, postmortem + action items for template compile cache and schema-size limits
Miguel: taking over. I'll run the cache canary and promote to prod if stable. will keep on-call loop updated. ETA 2h for full validation, will page if anything regresses.
Eli: thanks — leaving paged escalation to Miguel. if regression, page eng-sre and escalate to TL.
Kayla: adding follow-up tasks to the incident board: template cache, compile-time metrics, JSON-mode per-route opt-in gating, test harness for large tool schemas.
IncidentBot: severity -> P1 updated by Eli (customer-impacting p99 SLO breaches).
Miguel: final note before takeover: if you see streaming stalls still, force chunked streaming fallback (agent-sdk config) to avoid per-request blocking until templates are compiled/cached. I'll coordinate with SDK team if needed.
Jules (Support): I'll keep customers updated every 30m and flag any critical escalations. thanks all.
Kayla: good job team. logging this as active incident; handoff to Miguel for overnight monitoring.
IncidentBot: incident thread 1816363000 marked active; incident commander: Miguel
